issues.description: Project IDs are interpolated into URL paths without percent-encoding, so IDs containing slashes or reserved characters hit the wrong endpoint.
Project IDs in batch-create paths are not URL-encoded, allowing malformed paths for valid but reserved-character IDs.
Task IDs in annotation-list paths are not URL-encoded, so reserved characters can change routing semantics.
Annotation IDs in review paths are not URL-encoded, making client behavior incorrect for IDs containing path delimiters.
Retry-After parsing only supports numeric seconds and ignores valid HTTP-date Retry-After headers.
Backoff cap is applied before jitter, so actual sleep can exceed the configured cap.
Exhausted retryable 5xx responses raise generic LumenAPIError instead of preserving retry-exhaustion context.
Pagination silently treats successful malformed responses without an items field as an empty result set.
Batch-create trusts the response schema and does not verify result count, duplicate indexes, missing indexes, or invalid statuses.
BatchItemResult accepts invalid status values and inconsistent task/error combinations without validation.
ReviewResult accepts invalid verdict values despite the public type claiming only approve or reject.
The mock server returns an empty annotation list for unknown tasks instead of a not-found error, masking likely production failures.
Scripted mock responses bypass API-key validation, so auth-related tests can accidentally pass under unrealistic conditions.
The typed package does not ship a py.typed marker, so downstream type checkers may not treat it as a typed PEP 561 package.
